evidence: Overexpression of SFPQ Improves Cognition and Memory in AD Mice
In this study, an AD mouse model was established through lateral ventricular injection of amyloid-beta1–42 (Aβ1–42).
Subsequently, adeno-associated virus was administered to overexpress SFPQ in the hippocampus of AD mice.
The results demonstrate that SFPQ overexpression improves recognition and memory in AD mice, while reducing AD-related marker proteins such as amyloid precursor protein (APP) and Tau.
paragraphs: Mice provide the experimental model context for the study. The authors established an AD mouse model, overexpressed SFPQ in the hippocampus, and assessed recognition, memory, and AD-related molecular changes in these animals.

evidence: Splicing factor proline and glutamine rich (SFPQ) is known to play a crucial role in neurodegenerative diseases, including antioxidant-related functions and regulating gene expression within brain neurons.
However, the specific role of SFPQ in AD pathology is not well understood.
Subsequently, adeno-associated virus was administered to overexpress SFPQ in the hippocampus of AD mice.
The results demonstrate that SFPQ overexpression improves recognition and memory in AD mice, while reducing AD-related marker proteins such as amyloid precursor protein (APP) and Tau.
These findings suggest that SFPQ may serve as a promising molecular target for the prevention and treatment of AD.
paragraphs: The authors investigate SFPQ as the molecular intervention in AD by overexpressing it in the hippocampus of AD mice. They report improved recognition and memory, reduced APP and Tau, upregulation of synaptic, memory-associated, and antioxidant proteins, an increased Bcl-2/Bax ratio, and elevated PI3K/AKT pathway ratios. The findings position SFPQ as a possible target for AD prevention and treatment.
